text:
junaid: Quick follow-up on the quota-binding layers — we hit a weird case where per-tenant quotas are enforced at ingress but the downstream scheduler uses independent leases; results in double-counting and surprising drops. Anyone tried a single source-of-truth ledger vs passing tokens through?

tara: we prototyped a central ledger last year. Simplifies accounting but the extra RPC added ~6-8ms p99 for short requests, which mattered for low-latency routes.

ben: what about signed "lease tokens" passed from ingress -> scheduler? ingress decrements local view and issues token with remaining_units + TTL, scheduler redeems it. avoids a sync call.

carla: signed tokens sound neat but replay/forgery risk unless we have nonce or short TTL + jitter. also need a revocation path for cancellations.

junaid: agree on replay risk. also saw a variant where ingress does a "soft debit" (reserves) and scheduler does the hard debit on completion. if job is cancelled we reclaim the soft reserve.

matt: soft vs hard debit affects fairness: long-held soft reserves can starve others. we'd need a reclaim daemon and a reclaim metric pipeline (quota.reclaim).

ben: can combine both: short TTL signed token + soft reserve. token carries {tenant, units, exp, id} signed by ingress key. scheduler redeems; if not redeemed by exp, reclaimed.

carla: sketch of token payload: ```json
{
  "tenant":"acme-corp",
  "units":50,
  "exp":2141594850,
  "id":"tok-7f3a"
}
``` Signed with HMAC. Redemption endpoint validates sig + id once.

tara: still worried about centralizing revocation list size. If we store every id to prevent replay, that becomes big. Maybe use Bloom filter with TTL-based rotation for recently seen ids?

junaid: good call. bloom + per-tenant sliding window should bound memory. Also instrument: quota.issued, quota.redeemed, quota.expired, quota.reclaimed, quota.replay_detected.

matt: operationally, we need a graceful degrade: if signature validation service (key access) is slow, fallback to conservative local admission (deny or lower units) rather than blocking. add metrics for fallback_rate.

ben: abuse angle: attackers could craft many tiny requests to chew throughput; combine token approach with per-route leaky buckets and abuse-scoring. high-abuse tenants get lower TTL and stricter reclaim.

carla: important interface boundary: Keep token semantics small and stable: ingress only issues, scheduler only redeems/reclaims. Any other components should talk to a ledger service (read-only). That reduces coupling.

junaid: action items: I'll prototype ingress signing + scheduler redeem flow (PoC in k8s). @tara can you own perf bench (latency + p99) and bloom filter memory tradeoffs? @ben add eviction/backoff policy options to the admission API. @carla draft security checklist (replay, key rotation, revocation). ops-bot: create ticket? :point_down:

ops-bot: Created ticket PLAT-2742: "PoC: signed-lease-token flow + reclaim daemon" assigned to junaid, tara, ben, carla. ETA 2 weeks. :calendar: 

junaid: thanks — will post a short design doc + sequence diagram in #eng-platform when PoC is up. :thumbsup:
